summary: Malaysia’s ecosystem pledges are exclusively conservation-oriented. It commits to conserving at least 20% of terrestrial areas and inland waters by 2030 through effectively managed, ecologically representative protected areas and other conservation measures, making this a broad land-and-water commitment rather than one focused on a single land-cover class. Malaysia also aims to conserve at least 50% of forest and increase forest connectivity under the Central Forest Spine, Heart of Borneo, and urban-biodiversity initiatives; no deadline is stated for the 50% forest target. Forests currently cover 210,419 km², or 64.7% of Malaysia, so half of the country’s forest area would be about 105,210 km². Despite covering 32.6% of the country, agriculture is not explicitly included in a numerical ecosystem pledge.

targets.context: A broad conservation commitment covering terrestrial areas and inland waters.
Approximately 105,210 km², equal to half of Malaysia’s current forest area.
